story_text.value:
Fridge magnet shopping list on an M5Stack PaperMono (ESP32-S3, e-ink touchscreen), synced with a phone web app over Wi-Fi. Works offline, ~2,400 lines of C++.

This is a great wee device! BLE, Wi-Fi and LoRa on one board makes it flexible for way more than a shopping list, this is just what I built first. This firmware only uses Wi-Fi.

Fully vibe-coded with Claude Code, I didn't hand-write this. I wanted to see how Claude would get on with building something useful for a new hardware device.

As it's stuck to the fridge it's easy for the family to use, and it's already being used day to day which I'll admit is a first for a home built project like this

I build Suwu, which inspired by Omarchy — the opinionated, keyboard-first Arch + Hyprland setup from DHH and team. With that same spirit, Suwu aims to bring that same level of enjoyment to the web-based remote shell to dev machine, with only one single binary as a super easy deployment. story_text.value:
Hi! I am Hussain and I built Caspian.

For someone who vibe builds almost all the time, for both personal tools like investment or health dashboards or tools to help others, I found my projects scattered all over the place: researching with claude, writing context in notion, building with Claude Code, Devin, publishing in vercel, posthog for analytics and then others tools for GTM. Big part of brain energy drain was context switching, I wasn't very organized.

So I decided to build that lets me do all this from one place. I built Caspian. While most AI coding tools you use for vibe building stop at code, Caspian takes it all the way to users.

Caspian creates a "workbench" folder in your local machine where it puts all your projects so everything stays in one place and is also easy for your other tools to work with. There is a built in co-pilot, a context manager (.md files user can copilot both read/write), a one click publisher, analytics and an email outreach manager. Though the copilot uses API for processing LLM requests via open router (I make a little margin on top), it is pricy, so I build a standard "canvas" format that Caspian uses that your Claude/Codex or other tools you use also understand and can work with. Simply point them to https://caspian.md/docs and they'll learn to work with Caspian straight away, this is so that you're not tied to Caspian's co-pilot and if you prefer to use your own tools, you can do so.

Some other features I built around problems i found myself struggle with:

- Prompt refinement: Enter a vague prompt in co-pilot, caspian uses a cheap model to generate a detailed before starting the task.

- Preflight: It breaks down the task and tells you estimatedly, how much will it cost and how long will it take, before starting the task.

- Product and User context: Co-pilot has access to the two files so both you and Caspain has understand of your product and user.

- Code/No code: You can switch this button to dive into code or just stick with the vibes.

I hope it helps and you can build and launch a lot quickly. Feedback what's the most annoying thing when you vibe code?

title.value: Show HN: Caspian – Desktop app to build and launch small vibe-coded projects

story_text.value:
The world economy around us depends on complex financial work. How well can AI do it?

We(a team of ex-EY employees) built FAB - Finance Agents Benchmark, testing AI Agents on the work behind financial due diligence. Agents can find the relevant facts, but still struggle to carry them through to a complete, reliable analysis.

We’ll keep expanding FAB to more companies and testing more models. Building and running this benchmark isn’t cheap, so we’re scaling it in stages.

The benchmark is public.

GitHub: Hugging Face: https://github.com/SecondState-ai/finance-agents-benchmark data room and tasks: https://huggingface.co/datasets/secondstate/finance-agents-b...

I built Build-a-Date to help organise relationship date night plans. You create a list of options to do on a date then you can send it to your partner and they can pick the ones they're most interested in.

My partner and I have different organisation styles. I like surprises and to play things by ear where as they like to carefully plan thing out. So I built this to help bridge the gap a little.

Possibly this is of interest to very few other folks but since it doesn't really cost me anything to run I figure I may as well put it out there in case it helps anyone else :)

story_text.value:
Hi HN, I'm sushi. I built ParkourNote, a personal knowledge management app that currently focuses on research: finding papers, reading PDFs, asking AI about them, and writing.

A few things it does:

Describe a topic, and an agent creates a project, searches arXiv, and imports relevant papers The PDF reader previews citations on hover, overlays translations on the page, and shows original and translated text side by side The agent sees the page you're reading and your selection; you can also connect Claude or ChatGPT via MCP A block editor with math support that compiles LaTeX / Typst to PDF

Demo (7 min): https://youtu.be/yZs2nQJtgkg

ParkourNote is just me. I built it in about a month: the web app, a Flutter mobile app, and a Chrome extension. It isn't even my full-time job. I work on it for an hour or two in the morning before work, plus evenings and weekends.

Two things surprised me along the way:

- The web app uses BlockNote for Notion-style editing, but I wanted Flutter for mobile. I asked Claude to implement a compatible editor in Flutter. It took about a day, and it works: documents round-trip between web and mobile. - In high school I worked as a video editor for MarginNote. Back then, a single 5-minute video took about a month, from scripting to recording, editing, and animation. For ParkourNote, I made launch videos for the Chinese, English, Japanese, and Korean markets in one weekend, plus a second Chinese version cut for portrait viewing. I didn't open a video editor once. It was all done with Claude Opus 5.5.

PG recently posted something along the lines of: in the AI era, you want to be either very close to the users or very close to the intelligence. That resonated with me, but honestly, building this left me a bit lost. I find it hard to think of a consumer software feature that current AI can't build. So if anyone can build anything, where is the moat? I'm genuinely unsure.

The other side of it is exciting, though. Running ParkourNote alone, I feel less like a solo developer and more like a CEO of a small company: I manage product, engineering, marketing, and operations, and somehow it's all manageable. A one-person company feels genuinely possible now, in a way it didn't a few years ago.

Signup is required since the AI features cost money to run; new accounts get 100 free credits after email verification.

Happy to answer questions about the product, the workflow, or the moat question. I'd genuinely like to hear how others are thinking about it.

title.value: Show HN: ParkourNote – A research workspace, built solo in a month with Claude
